payload.checks:
18 checks in tests/i8d-brief.test.ts, authored against the DESIGNED API before any of it exists, and proven red at run-afe7d2f56851 - the failure is ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on engine/brief.ts, which is the honest red for a module that has not been born. Stating its limit rather than overselling it: a module-not-found red proves the checks run against nothing yet, not that each assertion discriminates. Each assertion earns that separately when the module lands and the suite goes green check-by-check.

EVERY IN-SCOPE REQUIREMENT, WITH ITS CHECK:

R1 absolute action URL -> 'every action URL is absolute http(s)'. Asserts answerUrl builds an absolute URL from base+topic, that a trailing slash does not produce a double slash, and - the part that matters - walks EVERY action of a real published card asserting /^https?:\/\//. This is the exact defect the owner witnessed: the shipped lane wrote 'answer:<topic>', which the phone refused.

R2 a gate looks like a gate -> 'titled, raised, tagged'. The title carries the iteration and the word gate, priority >= 4, at least one tag.

R3 action budget -> 'at most three actions, and the third opens the brief'. Asserts <= 3 (ntfy drops the rest SILENTLY, so an over-budget card loses the brief with no symptom), exactly 3 when a brief exists, and that the third is a view action carrying a fragment.

R4 the brief renders the decision -> two checks. 'the page carries the ciphertext and its own decryptor' and 'the brief renders the gate's own text, escaped' - the latter also guards injection, since a brief is ledger prose that may contain markup.

R5 the host holds ciphertext -> two checks. Round trip plus a word-level leak assertion on the payload, and a page-level assertion that the plaintext marker never appears while the ciphertext does, with the key read from location.hash - never the path or query.

R6 never announce an unservable page -> two checks. A store that never serves yields NO link; a served page yields a link whose key rides the fragment only, asserted by splitting on '#' and checking the base does not contain the key.

R7 a brief does not outlive its decision -> 'the ttl is bounded'. The requested life is honoured, and a wildly long request is capped at MAX_BRIEF_TTL_S.

R8 degrade, do not block -> two checks. publishBrief returns null instead of throwing when the store refuses; and at the lane level, a failing store still publishes a card carrying bless and dismiss, with the result naming the degradation ('degraded') rather than hiding it.

R9 publish iff the run would otherwise wait -> THREE checks, the heart of this iteration. (1) seWait on a live offer fires the park hook exactly once - the act of waiting IS the trigger. (2) Nothing else fires it: not a file wait, not an offer wait with no offer live. (3) A SOURCE-SCAN guard on bin/se-board.ts asserting announceOffer no longer appears there while pollAnswers still does - a poller cannot know the run's intent, but a tap must still land after the agent's turn ends. That third check is a standing structural guard, not a one-off: it fails if anyone reattaches the push to a timer.

R10 config read when needed -> 'the pairing is read at announce time'. A lane built BEFORE any pairing exists stays silent, then honours a pairing written afterwards with no restart - the exact scenario the owner hit today.

R11 the token stays put -> 'neither the log, nor the result, nor the brief'. Three surfaces, asserted by string search for the configured secret.

R12 an announcement is recorded -> 'success and failure alike, never neither'. Asserts an ok=true announce record after a success AND an ok=false record after the transport throws. This is the check that would have caught today's defect in a day rather than after one.

Q1 reachability -> carried by the R8 and R12 checks jointly: after an induced failure, either a card exists or a recorded failure does. The measure is asserted directly rather than left as prose.

PROMOTED SPIKE CHECKS, now permanent: the SP1 negatives ride as 'corruption is loud' (wrong key throws, tampered payload throws - GCM authenticates) and 'the key is url-safe' (40 seals, all base64url). They are the only guard between a shipped brief and a page that silently fails to decrypt on the owner's device.

D1 the tap - deliberately NOT automated, and the only one. It is the demonstration at gate_release, adjudicated by the owner from the phone. No test can stand in for a thumb on a real device, and pretending otherwise is what shipped the broken button.

ONE WORDING NOTE, recorded rather than buried: the register's R9 reads 'announce only when a human will adjudicate'. The owner sharpened it after the register was blessed - the test is whether the agent would otherwise WAIT, not who owns the decision. se.adr-announce-by-adjudicator carries the corrected wording, and the checks above bind to the correction, not to the older phrasing.
